principles.name: Balance
symptoms: Visual weight feels unintentionally lopsided; unrelated components dominate one side.
principles.mechanism: Large regions, high saturation, strong edges and detailed imagery can outweigh smaller simple elements; symmetry is only one valid balancing strategy.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Compare left/right/top/bottom mass using grayscale and thumbnails.
Move, resize or neutralize competing visual weights; rebalance with negative space rather than mirroring blindly.
Retest at mobile widths and with localized text length.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: A deliberately asymmetric editorial page need not be symmetrical; make asymmetry purposeful and stable.

principles.name: Contrast
symptoms: Important information or actions blend into adjacent content; all visual elements carry similar weight.
principles.mechanism: Differences in tone, scale, weight, shape, texture and hue make hierarchy perceptible; color-pair preference alone cannot establish accessible contrast.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Define foreground/background tonal relationships and deliberate hierarchy steps.
Use size, weight, spacing and color together; reserve accent for meaningful roles.
Run WCAG contrast checks separately for every actual text and meaningful non-text pairing.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: Decorative contrast cannot justify failure of required text or focus indicator contrast; do not claim perceptual contrast alone passes WCAG.

principles.name: Emphasis
symptoms: The viewer cannot tell which message/action matters, or a decorative element wins attention.
principles.mechanism: One dominant focal moment reduces competition; supporting information still needs a clear secondary order.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Identify a primary message or task action based on user intent.
Increase size, position, isolation or weight of that element before adding ornament.
Validate first-glance recall and that primary action remains findable in responsive layouts.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: Complex professional workflows may have several task-critical regions; avoid artificially demoting critical data to obey a single-hero slogan.

principles.name: Movement
symptoms: Eye path skips essential evidence or ends at an irrelevant decoration.
principles.mechanism: Alignment, directional lines, image gaze, contrast transitions and content sequencing influence scan paths.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Draw intended scan sequence through value proposition, evidence and action.
Align edges, use headings and spacing to create readable continuation.
Review in LTR/RTL and mobile orders; test visual scan separately from keyboard/screen-reader order.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: F/Z scanning is context- and script-dependent; eye guidance does not replace semantic DOM reading order.

principles.name: Pattern (Repetition)
symptoms: Cards, icons or sections seem unrelated, or repeated motifs overwhelm content.
principles.mechanism: Consistent recurrence forms rhythm and identity; too much sameness hides importance.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Standardize repeated component geometry, spacing and icon weights.
Add controlled breaks only at meaningful hierarchy moments.
Inspect pages side by side for consistency and distraction.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: Patterns are optional ornament; remove them if they reduce legibility, add motion overload or disguise affordances.

principles.name: Proportion (Scale)
symptoms: Headings, sidebars or media occupy arbitrary or implausible relative sizes.
principles.mechanism: Relative size ratios establish hierarchy and balance; modular scales ease consistency but are not mathematically optimal for all contexts.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Define a tokenized type/spacing/sizing scale appropriate to density.
Use flexible CSS constraints rather than rigid ratios and fixed-height containers.
Check long text, 200% zoom and narrow screens for loss of information.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: Golden ratio or rule of thirds are optional exploration tools, never accessibility requirements or universal aesthetic proofs.

principles.name: Unity (Harmony)
symptoms: Individually polished screens look like different products.
principles.mechanism: Shared decisions about color, type, imagery, spacing, radius and states give visual coherence across contexts.
diagnostic_tests: Check a full-resolution viewport and a reduced-size/greyscale view.
Describe the intended attention and information order before scoring the aesthetic.
interventions: Inventory repeated visual choices and identify drift.
Create semantic design tokens and reusable components before one-off styling.
Compare multi-screen screenshots; retain purposeful content-specific variation.
principles.counterexample_or_boundary: Uniformity is not the goal; different semantic states must remain visibly distinguishable and purpose-specific layouts can differ.
